title: Released TESS dip tracks have lower late ending rates, but do not establish that each structure becomes more stable
abstract: We test the survival of visible dip features in complex periodic variables using released TESS measurements. We reproduce all 4,210 source tracks, then select features after three detections using their early strength. Among 285 new tracks in 68 stars, the ending rate at 30-100 rotations is 0.195 times the rate at 0-10 rotations (95% star bootstrap: 0.100-0.391). With a separate baseline rate for each star, the ratio is 0.569 (0.319-1.184). Breaking links at 586 time gaps gives a pooled ratio of 0.239 (0-0.664), but leaves only three late endings. Thus the pooled ending rate falls, while a change within stars is not clear. A mixture of fixed rates can produce this decline without a change in each structure. This test separates future feature survival from the earlier pooled turnover scale of 132 rotations. It does not refute that scale as a descriptive mean. Selection, threshold crossings, merges and informative gaps prevent a direct grain lifetime measurement. Code, an original figure, source hashes and aggregate results are included.

display.caption: Ending rates after three detections and late / early contrasts. Pooled rates decline. Comparisons with a separate baseline for each star include a constant rate. Gap breaks leave few late endings.
